cohort: The study included 100 newborns delivered by elective cesarean section and 199 newborns delivered vaginally, all from first or second pregnancies and full-term, singleton births.
finding: There was no significant difference in 5-minute Apgar scores between newborns delivered by elective cesarean section and those delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: Although a higher percentage of vaginally delivered newborns (76.5%) had Apgar scores of 9 or 10 at 5 minutes compared to cesarean-delivered newborns (59%), this difference was not statistically significant.
